title: SQLAlchemy 2 ORM: working with databases

spans.text: SQLAlchemy maps Python objects to relational database operations. Its 2.x style uses `DeclarativeBase`, `Mapped`, `mapped_column`, `Session`, and `select()`. Scope sessions and transactions explicitly, handle failures, and never concatenate untrusted values into SQL. An ORM does not replace schema design or indexing.

spans.code:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class Device(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'devices'
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str]

engine = create_engine('sqlite+pysqlite:///:memory:')
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
with Session(engine) as session:
    session.add(Device(name='sensor-1'))
    session.commit()
    names = session.scalars(select(Device.name)).all()
    print(names)

spans.text: The session commits the transaction and returns query results as a Python list: `['sensor-1']`.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Install with `python -m pip install 'sqlalchemy>=2,<3'`. In-memory SQLite is for demonstration; configure production connections and migrations separately.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Scope sessions and engine resources correctly; test migrations and transaction behavior before production.
